# The proxy rule, one URL per line: "direct" (never through a proxy) or
# "proxy" (may use the person's proxy). Loopback (127.0.0.1, ::1,
# localhost) and plain http never use a proxy; HTTPS to a remote K2 may
# use the person's proxy. Read by k2_client::proxy_rule's tests (Rust) and
# tests/cli/proxy_rule_parity.sh (the CLI's bash and Python helpers), so
# all three give the same answers.
direct http://127.0.0.1:4646/cli/x
direct http://127.9.9.9:1
direct http://[::1]:4646/
direct http://localhost:4646
direct https://127.0.0.1:4646/
direct https://127.0.0.2/
direct https://[::1]/
direct https://localhost/
direct https://LOCALHOST./
direct https://app.localhost/
direct http://k2.example.com/cli/x
direct ws://127.0.0.1:4646/events
direct not-a-url
proxy https://k2.example.com/cli/x
proxy https://acme.k2.dev
proxy https://10.0.0.5:4646/
proxy https://[2001:db8::1]/
proxy HTTPS://K2.EXAMPLE.COM/
proxy https://user@k2.example.com/
